items.title: Louis Tio Interview, 1960-10-26
items.q: She's a very, very, very fine pianist. Oyama Johnson. She lives out here on Havana Street. But she never played in no band.

ctx.x: She's in Washington now. I think that's the one. That's right. She went to the Conservatory of Music. I believe Mr. Bollier told me he was there. What's his first name, Harold? You know, the pianist? He played cello and other obols.

Oh, yeah. That's, uh, that was another very fine musician. There was, uh, Bollier. Uh, now, another, another little fine pianist that she's teaching now, uh, Mrs. Johnson. She teaches music in one of these public schools. She's a very, very, very fine pianist. Oyama Johnson. She lives out here on Havana Street. But she never played in no band. But she's a very, very fine musician. A person that knows that whatever she reads, she puts it down. She knows what she's doing.
Yes. You say your brother lived there, too, on Havana Street?
